checks: Matched ad15334eed60c161 §§1–3, equations (1)–(6) and its binary product. For an integer reflection center, the retained mass is the sum of actual overlap lengths in paired fibers. Reflection preserves that submeasure, and a closed containing cap takes at least half via the pair of closed sides through the center.

Positive fiber indices are consecutive by convexity. Midpoint inclusion for the two endpoints gives a+c−b≤s≤b. Clipping the actual outer intersection gives exactly [min(a,c,s,a+c−s)]₊. When a+c>b, both remaining arguments are at least a+c−b. Exact rational overlap replay matched 2,695 compatible test configurations.

A heavy fiber, or a largest fiber among at most two, is fully retained at its own midpoint. With three strictly nonheavy fibers x=a+c−b>0 and x<2a,2c, so the lower bound at the middle midpoint is at least a+c>M/2.

The witness upper envelope is concave with the stated exact sampled intervals. At the middle base each endpoint overlap is at most ε and the self-overlap at most one, all attained at height 1/2. No extreme base can retain another positive fiber, so the maximum is exactly 1+2ε.

In each added binary coordinate a reflection about an integer coordinate preserves only the same value. Thus the retained maximum is unchanged under the product and the original mass is multiplied by 2^(n−1). The strict nonheavy inequality and limiting ratio follow with ε>0.

readability: The product calibrates sharpness of a possible 2^(−n) retention bound. The universal lower bound in this proof concerns one integer coordinate and at most three positive fibers.

summary: The midpoint overlap bound proves half-mass retention for at most three positive intervals, and the nonheavy family and its binary products have the stated exact reflected maxima.
